style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: The golden psalm -- a miktam, an inscription poem, David's creed of contentment that turns out to be a prophecy of resurrection. Its first movement is the settled portfolio of a satisfied soul: You are my Lord; apart from You I have no good at all; the saints in the land are my delight; the idol-chasers multiply their own sorrows and I will not carry their names on my lips. Then the inheritance language of Joshua's land-division applied to God Himself: the LORD is my allotted portion and my cup, my lot held secure, the survey lines fallen in pleasant places -- the Levite's confession that the Giver outweighs every gift. The practice that holds it all: I have set the LORD always before me; with Him at my right hand I shall not be shaken. And then the psalm outruns David: heart glad, glory rejoicing, flesh dwelling secure -- for You will not abandon my soul to Sheol, nor let Your Holy One see decay. Peter at Pentecost and Paul at Antioch both preached the empty tomb straight from this text: David died and saw corruption; the One who did not is his greater Son (Acts 2:25-32; 13:35-37). The last verse is the whole gospel geography: the path of life, fullness of joy in Your presence, pleasures at Your right hand forevermore.

1.text: A miktam of David, a golden inscription. Keep me safe, O God, for in You I have taken refuge.
1.amp: Michtam ['a golden Psalm', miktam, the KJV margin -- an inscription poem] of David. Preserve [shamar -- guard] me, O God [El]: for in You do I put my trust [chasah -- take refuge].
1.notes: miktam (H4387): by old reckoning a 'golden' poem, an engraving -- words meant to be cut into something permanent, which Acts proves they were. The whole request is one word, shamar (H8104), and the whole ground is one word, chasah (H2620): guarded because sheltered.

2.text: I said to the LORD, 'You are my Lord; I have no good at all apart from You.'
2.amp: O my soul, you have said [amar] unto the LORD [YHWH], 'You are my Lord [Adonai]: my goodness [tov] extends not beyond You ['apart from you I have no good thing'];
2.notes: The creed in seven Hebrew words: YHWH owned as Adonai (H136), my Master -- and every tov (H2896) in life traced to that one source. Not 'God gives good things' but the tighter claim: apart from Him the category 'good' is empty.

3.text: As for the holy ones in the land, they are the noble ones, and all my delight is in them.
3.amp: But to the saints [qadosh -- the holy ones] that are in the earth [eretz], and to the excellent [addir -- the noble, the majestic], in whom is all my delight [chephets].
3.notes: The company clause of the creed: the qedoshim (H6918) in the land -- ordinary covenant people -- ranked addir (H117), the word for nobles and majestic ones. Loving God re-prices His people (cf. Psalm 119:63; 1 John 5:1); David's chephets (H2656) follows his Lord's.

4.text: Those who run after another god multiply their own sorrows. Their drink offerings of blood I will not pour out, and I will not take their names upon my lips.
4.amp: Their sorrows [atstseveth -- pains, wounds] shall be multiplied [rabah] that hasten ['give gifts to another', mahar, the KJV margin] after another [acher] god: their drink offerings [nesek] of blood [dam] will I not offer [nasak -- pour out], nor take up [nasa] their names [shem] into my lips [saphah].
4.notes: The exchange rate of idolatry: another god in, multiplied atstseveth (H6094) out -- sorrows as the only guaranteed yield. David's separation is total: no nesek (H5262) poured, and the idols' shem (H8034) not even pronounced (cf. Exodus 23:13) -- the lips reserved for one Name.

5.text: The LORD Himself is the portion of my inheritance and of my cup; You hold my lot secure in Your hand.
5.amp: The LORD [YHWH] is the portion [manah] of mine inheritance ['my part', cheleq, the KJV margin] and of my cup [kos]: You maintain [tamak -- uphold, hold fast] my lot [goral].
5.notes: The land-division vocabulary of Joshua -- cheleq (H2506), goral (H1486), the allotment and the lot -- claimed for a portion no survey can measure: YHWH Himself, the Levite's inheritance (cf. Numbers 18:20). And the goral is not merely assigned but tamak (H8551), gripped: the estate is held by the Owner, not the heir.

6.text: The measuring lines have fallen for me in pleasant places; yes, the inheritance is beautiful to me.
6.amp: The lines [chebel -- the surveyor's cords] are fallen [naphal] unto me in pleasant [naim] places; yea, I have a goodly [shaphar -- beautiful] heritage [nachalah].
6.notes: The chebel (H2256), the boundary cord, falls where the lot decrees -- and David, hunted half his life, still calls the survey naim (H5273), pleasant. Contentment is here a verdict about the Surveyor, not the acreage: with YHWH as the portion, every parcel is prime.

7.text: I will bless the LORD who counsels me; even at night my deepest self instructs me.
7.amp: I will bless [barak] the LORD [YHWH], who has given me counsel [yaats -- advised, planned for me]: my reins [kilyah -- my kidneys, my inmost self] also instruct [yasar -- discipline, school] me in the night seasons [layil].
7.notes: Counsel from above, homework at night: the kilyah (H3629), Hebrew's seat of the deepest self (cf. Psalm 139:13), rehearses by layil what YHWH yaats (H3289) by day. A conscience tuned by God becomes its own night-school (cf. Psalm 17:3).

8.text: I have set the LORD before me continually; because He is at my right hand, I will not be shaken.
8.amp: I have set [shavah -- placed level, fixed in view] the LORD [YHWH] always [tamid] before me: because He is at my right hand [yamin], I shall not be moved [mot -- totter, slip].
8.notes: The psalm's discipline in one line: shavah (H7737), the deliberate act of keeping YHWH in the front of the visual field, tamid (H8548), continually -- and the yamin (H3225) position is the advocate's, standing where a defender stands (cf. Psalm 109:31). The un-mot life is a matter of where the eyes are set.

9.text: Therefore my heart is glad and my glory rejoices; my flesh too will dwell secure and confident.
9.amp: Therefore my heart [leb] is glad [samach], and my glory [kabod -- my honor, my tongue] rejoices [gil]: my flesh [basar] also shall rest ['dwell confidently', shakan, the KJV margin] in hope [betach -- security].
9.notes: Joy at three depths: the leb glad, the kabod (H3519) -- which the apostles read as the tongue -- exulting, and even the basar (H1320), the mortal body itself, pitching its tent (shakan, H7931) in betach (H983), security. The body's confidence is the hinge into verse 10: flesh can rest because of what God will not permit.

10.text: For You will not abandon my soul to Sheol; You will not give Your Holy One over to see the decay of the pit.
10.amp: For You will not leave [azab -- abandon] my soul [nephesh] in hell [sheol -- the realm of the dead]; neither will You suffer [natan -- give, allow] Your Holy One [chasid -- Your godly, covenant-loyal one] to see [raah] corruption [shachat -- the pit, decay].
10.notes: The golden line of the golden psalm: azab (H5800) negated at the grave's door, and the chasid (H2623) -- the covenant-loyal One -- kept from shachat (H7845), decay. Peter's Pentecost logic is exact: David died and his tomb 'is with us to this day,' so the verse awaited the Son whose flesh saw no corruption (cf. Acts 2:25-32; 13:35-37). The resurrection was in the Psalter a millennium early.

11.text: You will make known to me the path of life; in Your presence is fullness of joy, and at Your right hand are pleasures forevermore.
11.amp: You will show [yada -- make known to] me the path [orach] of life [chay]: in Your presence [panim -- before Your face] is fulness [soba] of joy [simchah]; at Your right hand [yamin] there are pleasures [naim] for evermore [netsach].
11.notes: The destination of the whole psalm: the orach chayim (H734, H2416), the life-path that runs THROUGH Sheol and out the other side. soba simchah (H7648, H8057), joy at saturation -- satisfaction's own word -- located before the panim, and naim (H5273), the pleasantness of verse 6, now at His yamin le-netsach (H5331), without end. The right hand where the Son now sits (cf. Acts 2:33; Hebrews 12:2).
